newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh rebels extend truce, agree to talk.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh rebels extend truce, agree to talk.

text.p: Rebels fighting for autonomy in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts have extended a truce and accepted a government offer for talks but want a later date for negotiations, officials said.

The officials said on Tuesday the Parbatya Chattagram Janasanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the rebel Shanti Bahini, said in a letter received by the government on Monday that the talks should be held on December 10. The government had proposed the talks be held on November 23.
The government is seeking to end the area's protracted separatist tribal insurgency that has claimed thousands of lives in the rugged Hill Tracts region .
"The government is considering the request for a change of schedule and would possibly accept it," one official told reporters.

"At the same time, the Shanti Bahini has informed the government through the PCJSS that it had extended the truce in the Hill Tracts, due to expire on November 30, until the end of December," he said.

The government endorsed a previous unilateral extension of the truce after October 31. "They (rebels) have extended the truce by themselves twice since October and we have not rejected it in the interest of peace," the official said.
The Shantis began an armed campaign in the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected their demand for autonomy.
They also want 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the hill and forest region.
Officials say more than 8,500 people, including rebels, soldiers and civilians, have been killed in the insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to seek refuge in India.
